utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. Will the Registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis, Aditya Menon, and our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, all. Vasvija Vidovic and Nicholas Robson for the Defence of General Rasim Delic, with legal officers Lejla Gluhic and Asja Zujo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Good afternoon to you, Mr. Begovic. Just to remind you, sir, that yesterday, at the beginning of your testimony, you had made an oath or at least made a solemn declaration to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. You are me reminded that you are still bound by that declaration to continue telling the truth. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Begovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I have a just a couple of follow-up questions on the third military action that you were for you testifying about yesterday. This is the action in September 1995. Do you know, sir, whether there were any units other than the El Mujahedin, other ARBiH units involved in the third military action in September 1995?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We heard that some other units also participated in that action.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember, sir, which other military units of the ARBiH participated in the September 1995 military action?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was a part of the 7th Muslim Brigade that participated on the other side of the river. Rumour had it, that is. And then we also heard that the 2nd Corps was to be in operation on the other side, on the other bank, but I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, for my own clarification, I'm going to interrupt. The first question was: "Do you know whether there were any units other than the ARBiH units?" And then the witness said, "Yes." The next question says: "Do you know which other military units of the ARBiH?" I'm not quite sure now whether the answer refers to the "other than them" or to "of."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Maybe -- I believe there's an error in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: My question-- the first question, sir, was other than the El Mujahedin detachment, were there any units of the ARBiH involved in the September 1995 military action?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the way I understand it, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Mujahedin is not being mentioned on the transcript again, and have you just mentioned the word "Mujahedin."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I see that as well. Let me try this one more time for the benefit of the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Other than the El Mujahedin Detachment, were there other units of the ARBiH involved in the September 1995 military action?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shall I answer now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we heard that there was a part of the 7th Muslim Brigade and that on the other side, from the direction of, I don't know what city, segments of the 2nd Corps also participated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Begovic. Now, immediately after the third military action in September 1995 was finished, where did you go, sir?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, towards the end of the day, I left for home.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And how long were you at home during this period after the September 1995 military action?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About seven or eight days, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And following that period when you were at home, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After a period spent at home, we returned to the area of Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask at this point in time that the witness be shown the document which has previously been marked as PT02949. That's PT02949, page 698. On the B/C/S, if we could please focus on the right-hand page of this document, please. The English version is actually page 4. Page 4 in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And while that's coming up, Mr. Begovic, do you see a document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Trial Chamber what this document is?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is -- these are some facts about me, personally; when I was born, where I was born, how much I spent in the army, what branch I belonged to, what my rank was, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know what type of document this is, sir?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I have never seen this before. This is the first time I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we please then go to the left-hand side of the B/C/S document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us what is written under Box 56 on this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It doesn't look like 56 appears even on the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At the very bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: There's a handwritten note.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It's at the top of page 4 of the English, but it's at the bottom of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there is something written, "the 29th of June," I cannot see the exact year: "Certificate issued on ..." I cannot make out the last word.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we please then go to --

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then above it refers to the year 1983.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we please go to page 697 of the B/C/S version. And if we could please go to the left-hand page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you know what the reference to those VJ numbers correspond to?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military unit, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you see the corresponding dates next to those military units?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those are the dates of stay in a particular unit, from which date to what date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's take a look first at the first listing on this page, let's take a look first at the first listing on this page; that is, 040492 through 310793. What military unit, sir, were you in during that time period?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And in the period, sir, from 31 July 1993 until 25 December 1995, what military unit were you in?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could then please go to the right-hand page in the Bosnian language, and if we could then just scroll over on the English to the far right-hand part of that page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic, do you see the "Box 44" that indicates ranks and dates?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, sir, is that information accurate?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about this particular piece of information, namely, that I was promoted to the rank of lieutenant, because that was not what was in my military service booklet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Begovic. Your Honours, we'd ask this document be admitted into evidence and be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, could you please explain to us what it is exactly that you're showing with this document, because it's not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: This is the military service records which were obtained from the Government of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I saw, on the front page, when we first looked at this document, that the witness did indeed have the rank of lieutenant; but on the document we have on the screen in front of us, where does the witness appear? Is that number his number there, which is indicated, 02011 and so on?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can certainly explain the layout of this document. It's a bit confusing at first. What these are are folders, file folders, with information printed on the front, inside, two pages, and the back. So when this was opened up and photocopied, that explains why you would see the first page is actually on the right-hand side, the page on the left-hand side is the back, and the two pages in the middle are facing each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So are we to conclude that what we have on the right side of the screen in front of us is the witness's military career, that he started as a sergeant and then promoted to a lieutenant in the ARBiH, and then a lieutenant in the Federal Ministry of Defence? I'm just asking what's the significance of the document on the screen which you wish to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We're simply, for the sake of completeness, showing this witness the entire document. If he indicates that he's unaware of these ranks, then certainly that might go to the weight the Chamber might want to give to the document. But this document is the official service record of this witness that was provided by the Government of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise if I stood up too early. I wish to challenge the authenticity of this document, and I should like to ask the OTP's office to make it possible for me to gain access to the original of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We can certainly do that, and I can endeavour actually to bring at least copies of what we have out of the evidence vaults perhaps later today or certainly tomorrow morning. We can make that available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. What response do you have to the challenge to the authenticity?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, again, I can be in a position to indicate exactly where this came from, but this was provided to us by the Government of Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. For my own edification, what we see on the screen, in the English language, is it a subsequent page of some document that begins somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me, if I can demonstrate perhaps graphically, what these are are file folders like you might see in a filing cabinet, and they're printed -- the information is printed on the folders. So the first page -- and perhaps we could go back to page 698. The page you see on the right-hand side in the Bosnian version, that page, is actually the cover of a file folder. The left-hand page is the back of the folder, because the folder was opened up and scanned electronically. The second pages, the pages 2 and 3, in effect, are the inside of the file folder which was then scanned, which explains why the pages are not exactly in the right order. Because in order to save paper and time, they simply opened the folder, scanned this side and then scanned that side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I appreciate that perfectly. My question relates to the English version. I'm asking, what we see on the screen now in the English version, is that a subsequent page of a document that begins a little earlier or is this the sum total of.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's the sum total of what was translated from that part of the service record book. And, again, if we go back to page 697, I think it might be -- it might be more readily understandable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Let me try one more time. What we see on the screen here, of what page of the B/C/S folder is this a translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It's on the right-hand side on the B/C/S version that you see on the screen, Your Honour, and it starts there are three handwritten entries, and those correspond to the three entries that you see on the translated portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And this page on the B/C/S is not the first page of the folder?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's correct. As you can see, it's Box 44; and perhaps if we zoom over to the other -- not the other page but the other side of this, you'll there see Box 43.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm now answered. Therefore, the English version does not relate to the first page of the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, it relates to Box 44.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And if we go to the first page of the English version, it will translate personal history of the accused and his names and everything?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So to answer Judge Harhoff's question, this document must be read with the rest of the pages to be able to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Exactly. The entire -- the entire file folder must be read together, and the best way of doing that is simply to follow the numbers in the B/C/S version, and then look for the corresponding portions of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, if I may just find out from you, you would like to be shown the original of this document, and Mr. Mundis says he can do so. Do you have any further objections to the document, or do you --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, Your Honours. I wish to examine the original, and I still challenge the authenticity of this document also bearing in mind the part of the witness's statement to the effect that he had heard for the first time right now that he had been promoted to the rank of lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. In that event, then, the document will be marked for identification, and may it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 78, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we could now show the witness -- well, before we do that, they could perhaps begin loading PT02796. PT02796.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And while that's being done, Mr. Begovic, what commendations or awards or medals or other honours did you receive, if any, as a result of your service with the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was awarded the Silver Shield of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, but I only found out about this decoration some two years subsequently later, because we didn't sit much store by that because we feel that each combatant was just as deserving. And I felt that to be true of my fellow combatants as well, if you understand what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic, do you now see the document on the screen in front of you, PT02796?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see your name on this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recognise the names of any of the other individuals on this document?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can you tell the Trial Chamber, sir, approximately where your name is located on this document?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards the end of the list, the third from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Begovic. Your Honours, we'd ask this document be admitted into evidence and be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is Exhibit 79, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: This completes the direct examination of this witness, Your Honour. Mr. Begovic, thank you very much for answering our questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Just one second. Please bear with me until I get organised. Your Honours, right at the beginning I will be asking just a couple of general questions that relate to the general situation and the general military situation in his area, because I believe that this is relevant to our case. So these would be just a couple of questions limited in scope. I just wanted to give you the heads-up on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will be asking you some questions today on behalf of General Delic, as his Defence counsel. I will be asking you the kind of questions that can, in most cases, be answered by "yes" or "no," and I would like to ask you, because I want to ask you as many questions as possible and our time is limited, to do so whenever possible, to say "yes" or "no," unless the Trial Chamber asks for some further clarifications or if do so. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since we both speak the same language, I will be asking you, for the sake of the interpreters, to make a pause for my question to be interpreted and then to give your answer. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic, in your evidence yesterday, you told us that when the war broke out, you were in Suhi Dol in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You explained to us that this was in the Travnik area, Central Bosnia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The non-Serb population outside of Central Bosnia came under attack in April 1992. The attack was launched by the Serb forces. You do know that?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also know that those attacks resulted in the expulsion of the Muslim population from large areas of Bosnia and Herzegovina where Serbs were in the majority; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: For all intents and purposes, in the first few months of the war in 1992, the area of Eastern Bosnia and of Bosnian Krajina, these areas were ethnically cleansed of the Muslim population; this is something that is general knowledge, is that so? This is something that everybody in Bosnia and Herzegovina knew?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that is indeed so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like a video clip shown to the witness. That's VD5, that's the designation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic -- thank you, yes, I understand. But for the purposes of this question, what we have just seen is enough. Mr. Begovic, the reason why I showed you this video clip is because I want to put it to you that the masses of refugees from Eastern Bosnia and from Bosnia Krajina, in fact, over-flew into Central Bosnia, where you lived, in 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we have the exhibit number for this video, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The video clip is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 80, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like another video clip to be shown to the witness. It's VD2. And at the same time, could we have the English transcript of this video. And the number of that document is D34.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I hope that you have been able to follow this in the transcript. Unfortunately, we've just -- we're just getting used to e-court, and we couldn't play both together. The witness heard the audio recording, and I would like to ask you the following question, Mr. Begovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We didn't have any translation, so we didn't follow anything except just to see a movie without words that mean anything to us. Is there any way that you can make us understand what was playing?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Even now the translation --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay, yes, I can see the transcript on my screen, but we couldn't have -- I hope that now you can hear me. I hope that now you can hear me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, we can hear you now, through the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the screen in front of me, I have the transcript of this video. It's in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Later, but all I'm saying is at this stage we don't know what took place because we didn't have the opportunity to read it. We'll read it later.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like the usher to assist me. Next time we want to play a video clip, I would like to have the transcript together with the video clip. But the most important thing of all is that the witness was able to understand it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you've seen this video now and you heard what this is all about. It's about refugees, more than 100.000 refugees, 186.000 refugees who came to Travnik from different areas in Bosnia-Herzegovina, including the Bosnia Krajina. This video clip that you just saw, does this reflect the actual situation in Travnik in the second half of 1992, all the way until the summer of 1993?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it does, yes. These were daily occurrences in the very beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Before the war, Travnik was a small town?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: About 18.000 people lived in the town itself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I don't think that there were more than 20.000 people there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in the wider area of Travnik, the Travnik Municipality, it was about 70.000 people?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, this man, he said that about 186.000 refugees had come to Travnik. You were able to hear that on this video; is that correct? Did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with an assessment made by this man as to the figure for the refugees, that really that many refugees had arrived?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably more than that passed through, because some went on to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It is true, is it not, that such an influx of refugees in fact paralysed life in this area; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you probably are, because these people had to be taken had care of, accommodation had to be found for them. Because even in our area in Mehurici, there were some refugees.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I would like this video to be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would ask that it simply be marked for identification until the Prosecution has also had an opportunity to review the transcript of the videotape.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, yes, definitely, I agree. It's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then the video will be marked for identification, and may it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As 81, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And I guess, Madam Vidovic, you would also like D34, the English transcript, to be given an exhibit number for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, definitely, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll do the same with D34, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. That will be marked for identification as 82.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begovic, I will now ask you something on a different topic. Up until the end of 1992, or thereabouts, there was no open conflict between Muslims and Croats in Central Bosnia. That's how I understood your evidence yesterday.

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the situation deteriorated significantly as the year 1992 drew to a close because of the Croatian Defence Council forces moving against the Muslim population in that area?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, now I would like to show a document to the witness. Could the witness please be shown document D8. For the record, let me just explain that this is a document issued by the Command of the 306th Brigade. The number is 02/98-5. It is dated January 1993, and it is entitled "Relations with the Croatian Defence Council, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna." In his evidence yesterday, the witness told us that he was a member of the 306th Brigade up until at least early August 1996.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that correct, Witness?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before I go on to quote portions of this document, I would like to ask you the following, or to put it to you the following: You knew that in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, a para-state had been formed by force, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and that it concluded parts of Travnik municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will quote a short part of this document for you, the document that you have in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that is the part of this document which is the second half of the document, which is the HVO command also, in addition, the HVO Command, Travnik, informs us about the order issued by the HVO command of the so-called Herceg-Bosna, regarding placement of the BiH army units under the command of the HVO, command of the HVO, command of the so-called Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in connection with this, Witness, I would like to ask you this: This document, it's content, this portion which I read out for you, reflects the events in the field in early 1993 in the Travnik area; is that correct? Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I haven't seen the document, but it is quite certain that the HVO did have aspirations on this area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about this part which I read, this information that I read out for you. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, we're trying to keep pace with you. The interpreter was speaking so fast that I couldn't hear what she was saying. I'll ask you to please slow down a little bit. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, I shall put this question to you again perhaps, perhaps differently formulated. Is it true that HVO forces in the Travnik area, in early 1993 and thereafter, tried to put the forces of the army under their control? Did you have that information?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe it was so, and the situation was similar in Mostar and in other areas where they were in power, where they had their Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may this document be given an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. But before we do that, madam, I don't understand your question. "Is it true that the HVO forces in the Travnik area, in early 1993 and thereafter, tried to control the forces of the army ...?" Which army?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the forces of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It was probably omitted from the transcript. That is what I said: The forces of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, to put those forces under their control.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, Witness, understand the question the way I just put it?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, madam. Well, the transcript is admitted into evidence, and may it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 83, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you agree that the Muslim population of Central Bosnia, because of these events, found itself in an extremely difficult situation?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: They fought for bare survival and they fought against two enemies: The Serb forces, on the one hand, and the Croat forces, on forces, on the other hand?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Otherwise, Witness, do we agree that Bosnia and Herzegovina itself was blockaded from the very beginning of the war partly by Serbia? Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you agree that already, as of the spring of 1993, it was also blocked by Croatian forces as well?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, Witness, already as of the spring of 1993, the boundaries of the borders of Bosnia and Herzegovina were blockaded by hostile forces; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I shall now just ask you one thing in reference to something which you mentioned yesterday in respect of the organisation of the brigade, and this is the question: The Yugoslav Army withdrew weapons from settlements in which there lived a non-Serb population also in your area; am I right?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: They pulled out different military equipment as well, did they not?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you told us that the first events in the war were when the Serb forces demolished the communication tower on Mountain Vlasic?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they took it. They took that feature. I don't know to what extent they demolished it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that explanation. If I put it to you that throughout the second half of 1992, in the area in which you lived, there, in fact, did not exist any organised military forces, would I be right?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was the very beginning of the organising, but they were not wholly regulated, that is for sure. It was more an organisation on paper than in practice, in establishment terms.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I was just about to refer to that part of your testimony so that we could clarify it. Yesterday, you said it was more on paper than in actual reality. Did I get you right? I understood that the unit in which you were existed more on paper than in reality. Is that what you wanted to say? Is that what you meant?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I meant that, too. We didn't have any arms. We didn't have any means, resources for warfare. It was just a plain guard. If one were to compare a company, a military formation of the rank of a company, and thus then we can say that we were not organised.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right, Witness, if I say that these were village groups or village armies composed of the local population in your area?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were organised primarily by villagers, so each village had organised its own guards of this sort.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: They did not have military experts who could establish an army according to certain rules; am I right?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we had no one of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I claim that the Muslims in your area very seldom had officers with a military education, that they there were military-educated officers among the Muslims, that this was a rarity?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are quite right. There was one from my village who had military education, but he wasn't with us during the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So even this one officer with a proper military education from your village was not with you during the war?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was not in Bosnia at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your evidence yesterday, you told us that the 306th Brigade was established in 1993 or thereabouts, and in this respect I want to ask you the following question: Would you agree with me that at least throughout 1993, this brigade operated in extremely difficult conditions?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were difficulties, I said yesterday, with the formation itself. There were difficulties. Some wanted to others didn't. There was haggling, there was -- negotiations were quite some time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I'll come to that later. Let me just ask you this. I asked you in general about Central Bosnia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the two fronts which it -- where the people had to fight, but now I want to ask you the following: Your own Brigade, the 306th, had to also fight on two front; on the one hand against the Serbs, and on the other front against the Croats; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right when I say that it had a huge front line, at least 45 kilometres long?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had such lines with the HVO when the conflict with them started, and we also had a huge line against the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will counsel and witness please not overlap.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you said that there were not enough weapons, and you also refer to that today?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And not enough equipment, either?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, the interpreter is asking you to please not overlap. Give each other space for the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. It's not my day today.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I should like you now to take a look at a video clip which is marked VD4, and at the same time, if that is possible, can we have the English transcript of this video which is numbered D35? So if that is possible, can we see both?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, it is not possible to see the transcript and the video material at the same time. What we could do is try to ask the interpreters if it's possible to give us some alternate interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Or could we have the transcript in the booth, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And for that reason, they need the transcript in the booth, if it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we shall try to do so in the future. This is a very short video clip which has just a couple of scenes. It is not even necessary to hear the text, in fact. But we shall try to provide this for the future. [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Commander, sir, is the only thing that the interpreter could make out. A salute to the combatants and a response from the combatants.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you just please go back to the first still and then stay there. I have a question in relation to it. Stop it, please, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, take a look at -- a hard look at this scene, at these people. I should like, first of all, to ask you: Do you -- did you recognise anyone in this video clip, if you paid attention?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people lined up here?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, among the commanding staff.

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps Remzija. I'm not sure. I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "Remzija," if I ask you, are you referring to Remzija Siljak, the head of the 306th Brigade, is that whom you mean?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I meant him.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Do you agree that the 306th Brigade, as regards uniforms, was when it was established and during 1993 that it looked more or less like shown in this video?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these were the people as they were, these lined-up people. They actually came in their own clothing. We didn't have anything else. When a suit came, that was later to the village, then people would fight over it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, can this video clip be given an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The video clip is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm awfully sorry. I'll say that again. The video clip, VD4, is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 84, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And I guess, Madam Vidovic, you want D35 also to be given an exhibit number. That's the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Registrar please do the same with D35.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That will be Exhibit 85.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should now like to show the witness a document, another document, and to ask him for his comment. This is document D10. For the record, this is a document of the 306th Brigade, strictly confidential, 02/348, of the 11th of April, 1993. Its title is "Operational Report" addressed to superior commands.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to quote a very short portion of this document. That is the second paragraph, Your Honours, more or less. Yes, this is it, where it refers to logistic support. Witness, I shall quote: "Logistic support of the unit is bad, which made it practically impossible for us to carry out regular jobs. The causes: The lack of fuel and lubricants and spare parts for vehicles. A constant problem has also been the lack of weapons, ammunition and the clothing, which we have already warned about earlier. Communication with the OG West Command has been practically nonexistent in approximately the past ten days. This should be solved immediately. The lines where the OG West Command are known are occasionally very bad so that it is not possible to check, let alone to work. "Therefore, we were not able to carry out your order number 01/74-93 of 9 April 1993. The reason is that we are 18 kilometres away from the Travnik Communications Centre and we have no means for sending a messenger three times a day." In this connection, Witness, I should like to ask you to clarify, for the benefit of the Chamber, if you are able to, it is true, isn't it, that also in the spring of 1993, in April, the brigade was still at the level of village units? This document says that; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the situation was difficult. Now, in organisational terms, how it was, whether it was exactly like this, I was still with my company at the time so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that company also functioned as a village unit, did it -- did it not at that time, as a village group defending its village?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the way it was up until these actions against the HVO. I believe that after that, the -- we had some different organisational rules, different organisation undertaken.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "this action against the HVO," what period are you referring to? Until what time did this situation obtain?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was referring to the situation where the fighting against the HVO started, and more significant moves in terms of improving organisation were taken after -- in the second half of 1993. I'm not quite sure, in fact, because I left for the El Mujahed Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. The purpose of my question is as long as you were with the 306th Brigade, in the company, your company of the 306th Brigade, was this the kind of situation which obtained until you joined the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, just to give you an example, perhaps, in the last three or four months, maybe from April until August, when I moved to the El Mujahed Detachment, I was some kind of a commander of the company, but it didn't really function in reality. We -- It was just on paper. We didn't have any materiel, any weapons. We held the line facing the Chetniks, the Serb aggressor. So it was only on paper. In practice, it just didn't function.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would that mean, then -- or rather if I were to put it to you that for that reason the brigade couldn't function, for all intents and purposes, would I be right?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was difficult for it to function. It was very difficult, that's for sure, for the reasons that we just mentioned and the problems with the HVO. We were in a very difficult situation. It was a "to be or not to be" kind of situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will go -- get to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: To make things abundantly clear, at line 23 on this page 29, when the witness refers to the period April until August, of which year are we talking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1993. Thank you, Your Honour, for your intervention and for the clarification.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this document, sir, it also says that the brigade was isolated from its superior command, that was OG West; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what OG West is, so I can't really -- I can't really make any comments.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Fine. In your evidence yesterday, you said that because there was no organisation, that this was one of the reasons that prompted you to leave the brigade, this total disarray?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please -- could this document please be given an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry for the interruption, Your Honour. As Exhibit 86.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It shall be Exhibit 86. What I was going to say was that there is the English translation of the exhibit. Is it given a separate exhibit number or is it an "A" and a "B" of 86?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The same exhibit. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, in the spring of 1993, all the way up to August 1993, you were in the 306th Brigade. You were in this area, generally speaking; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is true, is it not, that in April 1993, the forces of the Croatian Defence Council put up roadblocks on the roads in your area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, first, the conflicts broke out in Novi Travnik, and then it spread to other areas: Areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I would like the witness to have a look at another document, Your Honours. It is document D11. It's a protest sent by the 3rd Corps, dated the 13th of April, 1993, to the Monitoring Mission and to the HVO Command in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, let me quote just a small part of this document. I think that you will be able to assist us in this regard.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The third paragraph of this document. Your Honours, I'm trying to waste as little time as possible reading out those documents, so I will start out in the middle. It says here in this document: "Vehicles are being taken away at roadblocks manned by HVO; and on 13th of April, 1993, the HVO units blockaded the town of Novi Travnik. According to our information, the HVO forces are grouping, and Muslim civilians are being arrested. "On the 13th of April, 1993, HVO units set up new roadblocks and reinforced the existing ones, the Han Bila-Zenica road at Ovnak; the Rudnik-Nova Bila road above the village of Pokrajcica; the Rudnik-Guca Gora in Kosovo; and in front of Guca Gora, several roadblocks on the road leading from the village of Guca Gora to Travnik."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, my question to you, Witness, is: It is correct, is it not, that this document reflects the situation on the ground, the area where your brigade was operating was, in fact, criss-crossed with those HVO check-points?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, because Croat and Muslim villages alternated, and roads between them were blocked.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This made it impossible to move in this area, to move normally?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I would like to ask you, in this regard, is it correct that elements of your brigade were, in fact, isolated from each other?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document into evidence. Could it please be given an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 87, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your evidence yesterday, you said that the brigade command was located in the Bila Mine; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that this command remained there at least until the 28th of June, 1993, in the Bila Mine, that would be correct?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date. It was there at that time. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mean in June?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know the exact date, until what date it was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During those events, you said that there was an action in June that you participated in?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that at that time the brigade command was located in the Bila coal mine?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you allow for the possibility that it was moved to Krpeljici after that? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that Sipic was blocked in Krpeljici, that he couldn't leave. I don't know whether that held true for the whole command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you say -- you said "Sipic was blocked." When you say "Sipic," you're referring to Esad Sipic, the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you meant him when you said that he had been blocked in Krpeljici?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, he couldn't leave Krpeljici at all because of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much for the clarification. In your evidence yesterday, in answer to questions put to you by the Prosecution, you said that there was just one element of the 306th Brigade in the school in Mehurici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to put it to you that after the battalion of the 306th Battalion went into the school in Mehurici, the Mujahedin left the school and moved to the nearby village of Zapode, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the exact time when they actually left the school, so I really can't give you an answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly, you were not in the school yourself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would go to the school from time to time, but I don't know when -- when it was that all the Arabs left the school. I really don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I passed by the school, because it's very close to the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. I would now like to move on to a different topic. The time that you spent in the 306th Brigade, up until August 1993, you were in an area that was very close to the Mujahedin in Mehurici; am I right?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is true, is it not, that the elements of the 306th Brigade that you were in did not contain any Arabs who would be a member of that part of that unit; I mean, the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that there were any Arabs, members of the 306th Brigade, while I was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. We are talking about this time period while you were there, so thank you. Your brigade, the 306th, did not receive any supplies from the Arabs in any way; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it was supplied from them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It didn't get any weapons from them, did it?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that perhaps once or twice there was some training organised on a voluntary basis, ten or 15 people would go there, but that was the only way. There was no other support.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that perhaps some of the locals got weapons privately, in a way, not as an official member of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how that was organised. I know that they went there, two or three groups, but people would get weapons in all kinds of ways because there were no weapons around.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I will be showing you some documents later on, a document. In fact, I will be showing you a document right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could the witness be shown document D23? This is a document of the Command of the 306th Brigade. The number is 04/68-33. The date is the 30th of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I hope, Witness, that you're able to see this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please see the date on this document? Yes, yes. That's it. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You see the date here, the 30th of July?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, this is very close to this time period, the 1st of August, 1993, where, as you have told us, you left the brigade and joined the Arab unit. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me quote an excerpt from this document, a very brief excerpt.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is page 1, which you can see on your screen, the last two paragraphs on this page. The last two paragraphs on this page. Let me quote. The document says as follows: "Despite all this, we will encounter certain problems which surpass our capability and which have to do with the 1BB, where a significant number of people wish to transfer to other units, 7LKBR, because we are unable to provide them with weapons and to equip them, and they are not willing to hold the lines on axes outside of their objectives. "A certain number of fighters has joined the newly-formed El Jihad for other motives. There, they train, they are not on the line, they are financially stimulated, et cetera, while the huge area of responsibility, with 45 kilometres of front line facing both sides, remains there. And we find it more and more difficult to cover this whole area for the above-mentioned reasons and because we -- and for this reason we are mobilising everybody from 18 to 60 years of age."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just one clarification from you, Witness. The abbreviation"17LKBR," that could refer to "Light Krajina Brigade"?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, really.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you the 17th Light Krajina Brigade was deployed close to your area, is that right?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, some elements of this unit were deployed in our area, but I don't know if they were in our area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's fair enough. You have heard that the unit El Jihad is mentioned in this document. Would you agree that the group of Arabs that you joined at that time was actually called "El Jihad"? In other words, is it possible that you may have forgotten the name of that group? Does the name "El Jihad" ring any bells?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is what the locals called this unit at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the people just called them "El Jihad."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just let me clarify this. So this is the group that you joined in early August 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I should like to ask you this in that connection; namely, if I put it to you that the reason why Bosniaks joined this unit was the fact that that unit had something to offer to the fighters, for instance, it had training to offer?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It provided broad instruction, broad training on Islam?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, finally, that was one of the reasons, as you said yourself, why you joined?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those were my reasons.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It had financial incentives for the combatants and their families?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, occasionally.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Even before you saw this document, you had accepted the fact that the -- you had stated that the 306th Brigade was unarmed, and it was not organised properly. Tell us, Witness, was the 306th Brigade at that time at all able, in any way, to arm its fighters?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was very difficult.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, this document also referred to the fact that there existed voluntary transfers or joining of other units. So this document actually reflects the actual practice as regards these voluntary transfers; is that not a fact?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I am one of those who went of my own volition to join the other unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It is true, is it not, that moving over to the Mujahedins were not an exception? Is that a fact or not? This document actually refers to the -- to transfers to the 17th Krajina Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it does refer to that; and if the document says so, it is written there. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know that anyone from the 306th Brigade also went to join the 17th Krajina Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SINAN BEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anybody doing that. I don't know simply.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Your Honours, I should like to tender this document and for it to be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, yes, you are on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution does not object; however, I do want to point out that this document, D23, is the same document as one of the documents on the Prosecution exhibit list, and I'm wondering if the Chamber has any general guidelines with respect to that situation so that we're not, in the future, admitting the same document twice. It is, just for the record, it's the same as PT01433, which, of course, is loaded into e-court. And I simply put that on the record, if the Chamber wants to somehow give guidance for the future with respect to documents that might appear on both parties' lists to avoid any confusion down the road, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The common sense guidance is that we don't want to burden the record unnecessarily; so a document, if it's tendered by one side, the other side can use it without having to tender its own exhibit. Thank you very much. Document D23 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 88, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as you have informed us that we will be adjourning at 4.00 today, perhaps this is the right time for us to take a break, because after that I should like to present a document that will require more time. Perhaps I could stop with my cross-examination at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. In that event, then, we will take a break -- I beg your pardon. We will adjourn for the day, and we'll reconvene tomorrow again at quarter past 2.00 in this same Courtroom I. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 13th day of July, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.55 p.m.,
